content:
Hi everyone! We are happy to introduce our work "Compile to Compress: Boosting Formal Theorem Provers by Compiler Outputs" (https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.18587). We trained Kimina Prover Distill 8B and Goedel Prover V2 32B to self-correct based on Lean compiler outputs. We achieved state-of-the-art performance on PutnamBench among ~8B and ~32B models.

The models are available on huggingface: C2C-Kimina-Prover / C2C-Goedel-Prover / github repo

We are going present our work at ICML 2026. Feel free to reach out and chat with me! I'll be happy to communicate and share my ideas with you (about this work or other topics).

The self-correction mechanism looks highly promising. To some extent, it establishes a trust mechanism for formal theorem proving, especially when dealing with Lean formalizations spanning thousands of line of code. As an undergraduate student with a keen interest in formal verification, I am very much looking forward to your impressive presentation at ICML 2026!
